Cheap, measured, and currently making `packages/runtime` unable to host any artifact-loading integration test — worth queueing despite zero product impact because the next test author pays the same diagnostic lap otherwise (the error points at the metadata plugin, not the alias table). Dispatch scope: the one-line alias **plus** the card's own follow-through — evaluate converting the enumerated `@objectstack/spec` subpath list to the anchored-regex shape PR #8128 used for `platform-objects` ("one rule for every namespace… cannot go stale"), and sweep sibling vitest configs with the same enumerated list. The regex conversion is the actual fix for the class; the one-liner alone re-arms the same trap for the next subpath.

## Serial constraints — under the new same-package exemption

**Maintainer, 2026-08-18, verbatim: 「放开同包，同文件仍硬串行」**, granted on evidence measured today (#9460 and #9446 developed concurrently in `packages/runtime`, different files, merged 11:43:09Z and 12:28:20Z, no conflict).

⇒ Runs alongside #9462 (`endpoint-executor.ts`), #9416 (`domains/automation.ts`, resume block) and #9568 (`dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`). **All four regions are disjoint**, and this card's is the only one in the config layer rather than `src/`. ⛔ Same-file remains hard serial; none of the four share a file.

Four replacement rules carried into the dispatch: ① region surface · ② merge `main` before the PR · ③ merge again after a sibling lands · ④ conflicts to the merge queue, ⛔ not hand-ordered. ⛔ Exemption does not spread.

## ⚠️ The scope is NOT the one-liner — triage was explicit and I am carrying it verbatim

> *"Dispatch scope: the one-line alias **plus** the card's own follow-through — evaluate converting the enumerated `@objectstack/spec` subpath list to the anchored-regex shape PR #8128 used for `platform-objects` … and sweep sibling vitest configs with the same enumerated list. **The regex conversion is the actual fix for the class; the one-liner alone re-arms the same trap for the next subpath.**"*

⇒ Adding `@objectstack/spec/cloud` and stopping is the **wrong** deliverable. The enumerated list is the defect; the next subpath added anywhere reproduces this bug, and the diagnostic cost is the real harm — **the error points at the metadata plugin, not at the alias table**, so the next author pays a full diagnostic lap before finding it.

⭐ Same shape as three other findings this lane has handled today: a guard whose **population is enumerated by hand** rather than derived. If the regex conversion turns out not to be viable, say **why**, and the fallback must at minimum fail loudly when the enumeration goes stale — ⛔ not silently under-cover.

**Premise on `origin/main`**: triage re-routed this from a self-minted `domain:testing` label per the single-producer rule; the fix lands in `packages/runtime`'s vitest alias config ⇒ `domain:cli`. Type Task, zero product impact, queued because the diagnostic cost recurs.

Zone-2 assumptions, adjudicated:

- **"the ENOTDIR reproduces on current `main`"** — TRUE, reproduced before any edit.
- **"the enumerated list is the only such list"** — FALSIFIED in the useful direction. Nine configs carry it, not one, and four sibling configs had already been converted to the anchored regex — so the sweep's job was as much classification as conversion. The full 36-config population and its control query are in the PR body.
- **"PR #8128's shape transfers"** — TRUE, and checked rather than assumed: `platform-objects` needs its hand-written `/plugin` entry because that subpath is a FILE; `@objectstack/spec` has no such subpath, so the anchoring holds with no exception entry.
- **The card's own premise understated itself**: three published subpaths were missing (`cloud`, `integration`, `studio`), not one, and `integration` is already reached by `src/http-dispatcher.test.ts` as an `import type` — erased before resolution, so one deleted keyword from the same failure.

One conflict worth recording rather than resolving silently: the harness default asks for a model identifier in the commit trailer, while the dispatch forbids any model identifier in a pushed artifact. I followed the dispatch — `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, plus the session trailer.
